# Timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline }

```python
timelines.Timeline(
    length=0,
    unit=None,
    number_type=None,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    locked=False,
    meta=None,
)
```

A positive coordinate axis with events and nested child timelines.

A Timeline represents a temporal dimension in one of three domains
(Logical, Physical, Graphical) with either continuous or discrete
coordinates. It stores events in an EventData and can contain
nested child timelines (segments) at specified offsets.

**Intended usage:** This base class provides the full Timeline API but
does not enforce domain or modality constraints. For typical usage,
prefer one of the six concrete subclasses or the ``create_timeline()``
factory function:

- ``ContinuousLogicalTimeline`` -- beats, quarters, measures (Fraction)
- ``DiscreteLogicalTimeline`` -- ticks (int)
- ``ContinuousPhysicalTimeline`` -- seconds, ms, minutes (float)
- ``DiscretePhysicalTimeline`` -- samples, frames (int)
- ``ContinuousGraphicalTimeline`` -- cm, inches, points (float)
- ``DiscreteGraphicalTimeline`` -- pixels (int)

These subclasses restrict allowed units and number types to prevent
accidental cross-domain errors and provide sensible defaults.

Direct instantiation of ``Timeline`` is appropriate for internal use,
generic algorithms that operate across domains, or advanced scenarios
where domain constraints are intentionally relaxed.

If you have a ``Timeline`` instance and need the appropriate typed
subclass, use :meth:`to_typed`.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name          | Type                                        | Description                                                      |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| id            | [str](`str`)                                | Unique identifier for this timeline.                             |
| unit          | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`)     | The time unit for coordinates (e.g., seconds, quarters, pixels). |
| number_type   | [NumberType](`timetoalign.core.NumberType`) | The numeric type for coordinates (int, float, Fraction).         |
| domain        | [Domain](`timetoalign.core.Domain`)         | The temporal domain (derived from unit).                         |
| origin        | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`) | The start coordinate (always 0).                                 |
| length        | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`) | The end coordinate.                                              |
| is_locked     | [bool](`bool`)                              | Whether the timeline can be modified.                            |
| is_discrete   | [bool](`bool`)                              | Whether the timeline uses discrete coordinates.                  |
| is_continuous | [bool](`bool`)                              | Whether the timeline uses continuous coordinates.                |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Preferred: use concrete subclasses
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import ContinuousPhysicalTimeline
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=180.0)
```

```python
>>> # Or use the factory to auto-select the right subclass
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import create_timeline
>>> tl = create_timeline(loader)
```

```python
>>> # Direct base class (internal/advanced use)
>>> from timetoalign.core import TimeUnit
>>> tl = Timeline(length=100, unit=TimeUnit.seconds)
```

### add_child { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_child }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_child(
    child,
    offset,
    allow_expansion=False,
    use_conversion_map=None,
)
```

Embed a child timeline at the specified offset.

The child timeline will be locked after being added.
Parent-child coordinate conversion uses exact offset arithmetic.

The child's whole subtree joins this timeline's manifest, in which
every id is unique across all element kinds: an element of the
subtree whose minted id is already held here receives a freshly
minted one, and an element whose given id is already held here makes
the call raise without changing anything.

A timeline can accommodate events and other timelines, called
Children, as long as they use the same measuring unit.

When the child uses a different unit than the parent, set
``use_conversion_map`` to automatically convert the child to the
parent's unit via a C-Map. The parent must have a C-Map whose
``target_unit`` matches the child's unit, so that inverting it yields
the ``child_unit -> parent_unit`` conversion. The child's events are
copied with converted coordinates; the original child is NOT modified.

The converted child is named ``"{child.name} [{parent.unit}]"`` and
receives a minted id.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Default    |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| child              | [Timeline](`timetoalign.timelines.base.Timeline`)                     | The timeline to embed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | _required_ |
| offset             | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)                   | The start coordinate on this timeline, in the **parent's** unit. When ``use_conversion_map`` is set, the offset must already be expressed in the parent's unit (e.g. samples).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| allow_expansion    | [bool](`bool`)                                                        | If True, expand this timeline if needed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `False`    |
| use_conversion_map | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | Conversion map specification for unit conversion. Accepts the same formats as the ``conversion_maps`` parameter in timestamp functions: - ``None`` (default): No conversion; units must match. - ``True``: Auto-select a parent C-Map whose target unit   matches the child's unit. - ``str``: Look up by C-Map ID or target unit name. - ``TimeUnit``: Find by target unit. - ``ConversionMap``: Use directly. | `None`     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If child is not a Timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If units don't match (and no conversion map given), the offset is negative, the child is already a child of this timeline, an id given in the child's subtree is already held in this manifest, or this timeline is locked and the child would end beyond its length without ``allow_expansion``. An unlocked timeline expands to fit the child instead. |

### add_conversion_map { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_conversion_map }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_conversion_map(cmap)
```

Add a ConversionMap to this timeline.

Any map with a ``target_unit`` is automatically registered in the
unified timestamp system so that :meth:`get_timestamp` can resolve
coordinates in that unit. The map is stored as-is: ``TableMap``
instances honor their own ``kind`` (nearest/previous/next/linear)
and ``extrapolate`` policy directly, and analytical maps (e.g.
``ScalarMap``, ``LinearMap``) are likewise stored directly.

Several maps may target the same unit — a piece can carry two
readings of the same axis — and nothing is ever displaced:
the unit registry holds a list, stamps and tables show every
reading, and scalar lookup refuses to guess between them
unless the caller names one.

The map's id must be unique in this timeline's manifest: a minted id
already held there is replaced by a freshly minted one (on the map
itself), a given one raises.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                                     | Description               | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|------------|
| cmap   | [ConversionMap](`timetoalign.maps.ConversionMap`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] | The ConversionMap to add. | _required_ |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the map's source unit is incompatible, the map is already attached, or its given id is already held in this timeline's manifest. |

### add_events { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_events }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_events(rows, allow_expansion=False)
```

Add events to the timeline.

Only ``event_type`` and a coordinate are strictly required per dict.
Missing fields are filled in automatically:

- **id**: auto-generated (``e000001``, ``e000002``, ...).
- **temporal_type**: inferred from keys -- ``"interval"`` when both
  ``start`` and ``end`` (or ``duration``) are present, ``"instant"``
  otherwise.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| rows            | [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\] | List of event dictionaries. Required keys: - event_type: class name (e.g. ``"Beat"``, ``"Note"``) - instant: coordinate (for instant events), **or** - start, end: coordinates (for interval events) | _required_ |
| allow_expansion | [bool](`bool`)                                                        | If True, expand timeline if events exceed length.                                                                                                                                                    | `False`    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                        |
|--------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)     | If events exceed length and expansion not allowed. |
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If timeline is locked and expansion not allowed.   |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.add_events([
...     {"event_type": "Beat", "instant": 0.0},
...     {"event_type": "Note", "start": 0.0, "end": 0.5},
... ])
```

### add_external_references { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_external_references }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_external_references(rows, *, validate=True)
```

Append incoming external references to this timeline.

Rows are appended to the existing table; nothing is replaced or
deduplicated. ``access_points`` defaults to an empty list and
``comment`` to ``None`` when a row omits them.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                                                | Default    |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| rows     | [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\] \| [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) | Row dicts (or a PyArrow table) with the canonical columns ``event_id``, ``external_id``, ``access_points``, and ``comment``. Unknown columns are rejected. | _required_ |
| validate | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                    | If True (default), every ``event_id`` must name an event of this timeline's own event table.                                                               | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                             | Description                        |
|--------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------|
|        | [Self](`typing_extensions.Self`) | ``self``, so calls can be chained. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                    |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If ``validate`` is True and one or more ``event_id`` values are absent from this timeline's events. The message names all missing ids, sorted. |
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If a row or an access point has the wrong type.                                                                                                |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If a row carries unknown columns or ill-typed values.                                                                                          |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.add_external_references([
...     {
...         "event_id": "e1",
...         "external_id": "p2",
...         "access_points": [
...             {"uri": "Analisi_1/L1.pnml", "kind": "relative_path"}
...         ],
...         "comment": "Analisi_1_L1_A",
...     }
... ])
```

### add_flow_map { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_flow_map }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_flow_map(flow_map, id=None)
```

Add a FlowMap to this timeline.

FlowMaps enable coordinate transformation for timelines with flow
control (repeats, jumps, D.S., D.C., etc.). They are created by
`timetoalign.ScoreFlowController` and added to the timeline for
later use.

Design Decision: Timelines store FlowMaps, NOT FlowControllers.
FlowControllers are factories that produce FlowMaps.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                 | Description                                                                                           | Default    |
|----------|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| flow_map | \'FlowMap\'          | The FlowMap to add.                                                                                   | _required_ |
| id       | [str](`str`) \| None | Identifier for this FlowMap. If None, uses flow_map.id. Common values: "default", "atomic", "single". | `None`     |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> controller = ScoreFlowController(measure_data)
>>> flow_map = controller.create_flow_map()
>>> timeline.add_flow_map(flow_map)
>>> timeline.get_flow_map("default")  # Retrieve later
FlowMap(default: 5 sections)
```

### add_region { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_region }

```python
timelines.Timeline.add_region(region)
```

Attach a pre-existing Region object to this timeline.

The region's id must be unique in this timeline's manifest: a minted
id already held there is replaced by a freshly minted one, a given
one raises.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description           | Default    |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|------------|
| region | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | The Region to attach. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description                                                   |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | The stored Region: *region* itself, or a copy under the newly |
|        | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | minted id.                                                    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the region's unit does not match the timeline's unit, or its given id is already held in this manifest. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> r = Region(Coordinate(10, TimeUnit.seconds),
...            Coordinate(30, TimeUnit.seconds), name="Chorus")
>>> tl.add_region(r)
```

### append_child { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.append_child }

```python
timelines.Timeline.append_child(child, *, name=None, uid=None)
```

Append a child timeline at the current end of this timeline.

The child is placed at ``offset = self.length``, so successive calls
stack children end-to-end and expand this timeline. Because the child
is a fresh, unlocked timeline, its identity may be set here: *uid*
becomes the child's ID (the key under which it is stored and
retrieved) and *name* its human-readable name — both applied before
the child is locked by :meth:`add_child`.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                 | Description                                                                        | Default    |
|--------|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| child  | \'Timeline\'         | The timeline to append. Must be fresh (parentless) and share this timeline's unit. | _required_ |
| name   | [str](`str`) \| None | Human-readable name for the child. Applied when given.                             | `None`     |
| uid    | [str](`str`) \| None | Identifier for the child; also the key for :meth:`get_child`. Applied when given.  | `None`     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                 |
|--------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)       | If child is not a Timeline. |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)     | If units don't match.       |
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If this timeline is locked. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> parent = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=0)
>>> parent.append_child(
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=8), uid="A", name="A"
... )
>>> parent.append_child(
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=8), uid="B", name="B"
... )
>>> parent.list_children()
['A', 'B']
>>> float(parent.get_child_offset("B").value)
8.0
```

### apply_flow { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.apply_flow }

```python
timelines.Timeline.apply_flow(
    id='default',
    *,
    include_children=True,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    fill_gaps=False,
)
```

Yield the unfolded timeline for an attached FlowMap.

Slices this timeline at each of the attached FlowMap's sections and
places the slices, in target (unfolded) order, as children of a new
timeline of this timeline's **same concrete type**. Each section also
becomes a matching named Region on the result, in unfolded
coordinates.

Each slice sits at its section's target coordinate. Ordinary
concatenating FlowMaps stack the slices end to end; a FlowMap that
places its spans apart — a restored cut, or any FlowMap's
:meth:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.FlowMap.inverse` — leaves the
result empty between them.

Each appended child takes the source section's label as its id and
name — the id of the region a played span was built from — and the
Region marking it in the result takes that label as its name (its id
is minted). A span visited more than once (a repeat) is suffixed
``-rend2``, ``-rend3`` … so every child has a unique id. Section events live in the appended children;
the flattened coordinates remain reachable via
``get_events(include_children=True)``.

The returned timeline carries a reverse FlowMap (id ``"source"``) for
tracing coordinates back to the folded source, plus the forward
FlowMap (id ``f"forward_{flow_map.id}"``).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default     |
|------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| id               | [str](`str`)         | Which attached FlowMap to unfold along. Passed positionally, so ``timeline.apply_flow("A8")`` selects the FlowMap stored under ``"A8"``.                                                                                             | `'default'` |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)       | If True (default), child timelines are recursively sliced and included in each section.                                                                                                                                              | `True`      |
| uid              | [str](`str`) \| None | Optional identifier for the returned timeline.                                                                                                                                                                                       | `None`      |
| name             | [str](`str`) \| None | Optional name for the returned timeline. Defaults to ``f"{self.name}_unfolded"``.                                                                                                                                                    | `None`      |
| fill_gaps        | [bool](`bool`)       | If True, each hole between the placed spans becomes an empty child (plus a matching Region), so the result tiles its axis contiguously. Required when this timeline is a ``SegmentLine``, which admits no gaps between its segments. | `False`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                      |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The unfolded timeline (same concrete type as ``self``), with one |
|        | \'Timeline\' | child and matching Region per played section, each placed at its |
|        | \'Timeline\' | target coordinate.                                               |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                  |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If no FlowMap with the given id is attached. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> child.create_flow_map(["A8_1", "A8_2"], id="A8")
FlowMap(A8: 2 sections)
>>> unfolded = child.apply_flow("A8")
>>> unfolded.n_children
2
>>> unfolded.list_children()
['A8_1', 'A8_2']
>>> # Applying the inverse puts the spans back where they came
>>> # from, restoring the hole the cut left:
>>> restored = unfolded.apply_flow("source")
>>> float(restored.get_child_offset("A8_2").value)
129.0
```

timelines.Timeline.convert_to(values, target_unit)

Can be: - Scalar (int, float, Fraction): Returns a Coordinate object - Coordinate: Returns a Coordinate object - numpy array: Returns a numpy array of converted values | _required_ |

|        | [Coordinate](`timetoalign.core.Coordinate`) \| [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | - For array input: numpy array of converted values                  |

>>> arr = timeline.convert_to(np.array([100, 200]), "inches")

### create_child { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_child }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_child(
    length,
    offset=0,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    allow_expansion=False,
    child_class=None,
)
```

Create and embed a child selected by this timeline's spawn hook.

By default, this is equivalent to:

    child_type = parent._spawn_class()
    child = child_type(length=length, unit=parent.unit, uid=uid, name=name)
    parent.add_child(child, offset=offset)

``child_class=Timeline`` deliberately selects the experimental base class.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                | Description                                              | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| length          | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | Child length in the parent's unit.                       | _required_ |
| offset          | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | Child start coordinate. Defaults to zero.                | `0`        |
| uid             | [str](`str`) \| None                                | Unique identifier for the child. Auto-generated if None. | `None`     |
| name            | [str](`str`) \| None                                | Human-readable name for the child.                       | `None`     |
| allow_expansion | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True, expand the parent when needed.                  | `False`    |
| child_class     | [type](`type`)\[\'Timeline\'\] \| None              | Explicit class override for the child.                   | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                    |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The newly created and embedded child Timeline. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                             |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If coordinates are invalid or the child exceeds bounds. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> parent = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=8)
>>> child = parent.create_child(length=4)
>>> type(child) is ContinuousLogicalTimeline
True
```

### create_child_from_region { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_child_from_region }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_child_from_region(
    region_id,
    *,
    copy_events=True,
    uid=None,
)
```

Create a child timeline from a region (partitioning).

The child's length = region duration, offset = region start.
The child's class matches the parent's concrete class, and its name
is the region's name. If copy_events, events in [start, end) are
copied with adjusted coordinates.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                 | Description                                  | Default    |
|-------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------|------------|
| region_id   | [str](`str`)         | Id of an existing region.                    | _required_ |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)       | Copy events within the region to the child.  | `True`     |
| uid         | [str](`str`) \| None | Explicit child ID. When None, one is minted. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                    |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The newly created and attached child timeline. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description             |
|--------|--------------------------------|-------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)         | If region_id not found. |
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If timeline is locked.  |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.create_regions_by_splitting("breaks", prefix="movement")
>>> mov4 = tl.create_child_from_region("region_4")
>>> mov4.name
'movement_4'
```

### create_flow_map { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_flow_map }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_flow_map(
    intervals,
    *,
    id='default',
    at=None,
    target_length=None,
)
```

Construct a FlowMap from interval-like descriptors, attach it, return it.

Mirrors the ``create_*`` verb×noun convention (as in
:meth:`create_region` and :meth:`create_regions_from_boundaries`):
it constructs the FlowMap, attaches it to this timeline under *id*,
and returns it.

By default the played spans described by *intervals* concatenate
contiguously in the unfolded (target) axis; coordinates falling in a
gap between spans map to nothing (an empty ``unfold_coordinate``
result).

To lay the spans out with holes between them instead — which is what
restoring a cut needs — state the placement in any of three ways: mix
:class:`~timetoalign.timelines.flow.Gap` entries into *intervals*,
give each span its target coordinate in *at*, or pass *intervals* as a
``{target coordinate -> span}`` mapping.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type                                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Default     |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| intervals     | [Any](`typing.Any`)                                         | One interval-like descriptor, a collection of them, or a ``{target coordinate -> span}`` mapping. Accepted descriptor forms are region ids (``str``, resolved via :meth:`get_region`), ``Region`` objects, ``(start, end)`` coordinate pairs, ``Timeline`` objects, and interval events. ``Gap`` entries may be mixed into a collection to space the spans apart. | _required_  |
| id            | [str](`str`)                                                | Identifier for the FlowMap. Defaults to ``"default"``.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `'default'` |
| at            | \'Sequence\[Any\] \| None\'                                 | Target coordinate for each played span, in the order given. One entry per span, or ``None`` for a span that should follow its predecessor. Cannot be combined with ``Gap`` entries.                                                                                                                                                                               | `None`      |
| target_length | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| None | Total extent of the unfolded axis. Needed only when the flow ends in a gap, which no section would imply.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `None`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type        | Description                                               |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'FlowMap\' | The constructed FlowMap (also attached to this timeline). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> child.create_flow_map(["A8_1", "A8_2"], id="A8")
FlowMap(A8: 2 sections)
>>> child.create_flow_map([(0, 123), (129, child.length)], id="A8")
FlowMap(A8: 2 sections)
>>> # Restore the two skipped measures as a 6-quarter hole:
>>> child.create_flow_map(["A8_1", Gap(6), "A8_2"], id="restored")
FlowMap(restored: 2 sections, 1 gap)
>>> # The same placement, stated as coordinates:
>>> child.create_flow_map(["A8_1", "A8_2"], at=[0, 129], id="restored")
FlowMap(restored: 2 sections, 1 gap)
>>> # ... or as a mapping pairing each coordinate with its span:
>>> child.create_flow_map({0: "A8_1", 129: "A8_2"}, id="restored")
FlowMap(restored: 2 sections, 1 gap)
```

### create_region { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_region }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_region(start, end, *, id=None, name=None, meta=None)
```

Create a new Region and attach it to this timeline.

Under the unified verb×noun API, ``create`` constructs a new object,
attaches it, and returns it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                        | Description                                                                                              | Default    |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| start  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)         | Start coordinate.                                                                                        | _required_ |
| end    | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)         | End coordinate (must be >= start).                                                                       | _required_ |
| id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                        | The region's id, kept verbatim. When None, ``region_{N}`` is minted, unique in this timeline's manifest. | `None`     |
| name   | [str](`str`) \| None                                        | Optional display name; names may repeat.                                                                 | `None`     |
| meta   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | Optional metadata dictionary.                                                                            | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description                |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
|        | [Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`) | The created Region object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                      |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the given id is already held in this manifest or end < start. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.create_region(10.0, 30.0, name="Chorus")
>>> tl.create_region(30.0, 50.0, id="verse", meta={"repeat": 2})
```

### create_regions_by_grouping { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_grouping }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_grouping(field, *, name_format='{value}')
```

Create regions by grouping *adjacent* events on a field value.

For each *run* of consecutive events that share the same value in the
specified field, creates a region spanning the run's coordinate extent
``[min_start, max_end)``. Only adjacent events with the same value are
grouped — non-adjacent occurrences of the same value produce separate
regions, which may share a name; their ids are minted.

This "run-length" semantics is essential for musical data where, e.g.,
the same time signature may recur after a change (4/4 → 3/4 → 4/4)
and each occurrence should be its own region.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                                                                                                   | Default     |
|-------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| field       | [str](`str`) | Event field name to group by.                                                                                 | _required_  |
| name_format | [str](`str`) | Format string. Placeholders: {value}, {i} (0-based), {n} (1-based), {run} (1-based run index for this value). | `'{value}'` |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                         |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of Region objects ordered by start coordinate. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                        |
|--------|----------------------------|------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If field does not exist in events. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Time-signature regions (adjacent grouping)
>>> tl.create_regions_by_grouping("timesig")
[Region('region_1', name='4/4', 0-64 quarters),
 Region('region_2', name='3/4', 64-88 quarters),
 Region('region_3', name='4/4', 88-120 quarters)]
```

### create_regions_by_splitting { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_splitting }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_by_splitting(
    predicate,
    *,
    names=None,
    name_format='{prefix}_{n}',
    prefix='section',
    include_before_first=True,
    include_after_last=True,
)
```

Create contiguous regions by splitting at events matching a predicate.

Finds events matching the predicate, uses their coordinates as split
points, creates contiguous regions between consecutive split points.

The predicate can be:
- A string: field name. Events where this field is truthy (non-null,
  non-empty, non-zero) are split points.
- A dict: keyword filters in the same style as ``EventData.filter()``.
  For example ``{"breaks": "section"}`` selects events whose ``breaks``
  field equals ``"section"``.
- A callable: receives event dict, returns True for split points.

For each matching event the split coordinate is the event's ``end``
(interval events) or ``start``/``instant`` (instant events).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                 | Type                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                          | Default          |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| predicate            | [str](`str`) \| [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| [Callable](`collections.abc.Callable`)\[\[[dict](`dict`)\], [bool](`bool`)\] | Field name, filter dict, or callable identifying split-point events. | _required_       |
| names                | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                                                                      | Explicit region names.                                               | `None`           |
| name_format          | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                        | Format string. Placeholders: {prefix}, {i}, {n}.                     | `'{prefix}_{n}'` |
| prefix               | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                        | Prefix for auto-generated names.                                     | `'section'`      |
| include_before_first | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                      | Create a region from timeline origin to first split point.           | `True`           |
| include_after_last   | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                      | Create a region from last split point to timeline end.               | `True`           |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                            |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of contiguous Region objects in coordinate order. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Split at section breaks
>>> tl.create_regions_by_splitting("breaks", prefix="movement")
```

```python
>>> # Split at specific break types
>>> tl.create_regions_by_splitting(
...     {"breaks": "section"}, prefix="movement"
... )
```

### create_regions_from_boundaries { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_regions_from_boundaries }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_regions_from_boundaries(
    boundaries,
    *,
    names=None,
    name_format='{prefix}_{n}',
    prefix='section',
)
```

Create contiguous regions from boundary coordinates.

Given k+1 sorted boundary coordinates, creates k regions where
region_i spans [boundaries[i], boundaries[i+1]). The names label the
regions; their ids are minted.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                                          | Description                                                                   | Default          |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| boundaries  | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)\] | k+1 monotonically increasing coordinates.                                     | _required_       |
| names       | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                | Explicit names for the k regions. Mutually exclusive with name_format/prefix. | `None`           |
| name_format | [str](`str`)                                                                                  | Format string. Placeholders: {prefix}, {i} (0-based), {n} (1-based).          | `'{prefix}_{n}'` |
| prefix      | [str](`str`)                                                                                  | Prefix for auto-generated names.                                              | `'section'`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of k Region objects in boundary order. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If fewer than 2 boundaries or not monotonically increasing. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl.create_regions_from_boundaries(
...     [0, 30, 60, 90],
...     prefix="movement",
... )
[Region('region_1', name='movement_1', 0-30 quarters),
 Region('region_2', name='movement_2', 30-60 quarters),
 Region('region_3', name='movement_3', 60-90 quarters)]
```

### create_segment_line { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line }

```python
timelines.Timeline.create_segment_line(boundaries, *, copy_events=True)
```

Create a SegmentLine by segmenting at boundary coordinates.

Given k+1 sorted coordinates, produces a new SegmentLine with k
contiguous segments. Each segment's class matches self's class.

Does NOT modify self. Returns a new independent SegmentLine.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                                          | Description                                 | Default    |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------|
| boundaries  | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)\] | k+1 monotonically increasing coordinates.   | _required_ |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                | Copy events into their respective segments. | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type            | Description                        |
|--------|-----------------|------------------------------------|
|        | \'SegmentLine\' | A new SegmentLine with k segments. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If fewer than 2 boundaries or not monotonically increasing. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> measures = audio_tl.create_segment_line(

### derive { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.derive }

```python
timelines.Timeline.derive(target_unit, name=None, copy_events=False)
```

Create a derivative timeline in a different unit via C-Map conversion.

A ConversionMap implies the presence of a derived timeline in the
target unit. The derive() method makes this implicit timeline explicit.

The derived timeline:
- Has coordinates in the target unit
- Has length equal to the converted source length
- Automatically has an inverse C-Map back to the source unit
- Optionally copies and converts events from the source

This operation creates a NEW timeline, NOT a child timeline.
The source and derived timelines have different units, so per TTA
specification, they cannot be parent-child (children must share
the parent's unit). Use TimelineGroup to connect them.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                    | Description                                               | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| target_unit | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) | The unit for the derived timeline.                        | _required_ |
| name        | [str](`str`) \| None                                    | Optional name for the derived timeline.                   | `None`     |
| copy_events | [bool](`bool`)                                          | If True, copy and convert events to the derived timeline. | `False`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                        |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | A new Timeline in the target unit. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If no C-Map exists for the target unit.            |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If C-Map is not invertible (needed for roundtrip). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Create physical timeline with tempo C-Map
>>> audio = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=60.0)
>>> audio.add_conversion_map(LinearMap(2.0, 0.0,
...     source_unit=TimeUnit.seconds, target_unit=TimeUnit.quarters))
>>> # Derive a logical timeline
>>> score = audio.derive(TimeUnit.quarters, name="score")
>>> score.unit
TimeUnit.quarters
>>> score.length
Coordinate(120.0, quarters)  # 60 seconds * 2 q/s
```

### export_to_csv { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.export_to_csv }

```python
timelines.Timeline.export_to_csv(
    filepath,
    at=None,
    conversion_maps=True,
    recursion_limit=None,
    include_events=True,
    include_boundaries=False,
    *,
    fields=None,
    units=True,
    sep=',',
    header=True,
    index=False,
)
```

Export timeline data to a CSV file.

This is a convenience method that generates a timestamp DataFrame and
writes it to a CSV file. For more control over the output, use
``get_timestamp_table(format="dataframe")`` and save manually.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                     | Default    |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| filepath           | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Output CSV file path.                                           | _required_ |
| at                 | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) \| None | Explicit positions or event IDs to use as the axis.             | `None`     |
| conversion_maps    | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                               | C-Maps to include as additional fields. Defaults to True (all). | `True`     |
| recursion_limit    | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Maximum depth for child traversal.                              | `None`     |
| include_events     | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True and ``at`` is None, extract from events.                | `True`     |
| include_boundaries | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True, include timeline boundary coordinates.                 | `False`    |
| fields             | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\'                                                                                                                                                           | How to name the DataFrame fields (see get_timestamp_table).     | `None`     |
| units              | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True (default), append units to field names.                 | `True`     |
| sep                | [str](`str`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Field separator. Default "," (comma).                           | `','`      |
| header             | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True (default), write field headers.                         | `True`     |
| index              | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True, write row indices. Default False.                      | `False`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description             |
|--------|--------------|-------------------------|
|        | [int](`int`) | Number of rows written. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from timetoalign.core import TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> timeline = Timeline(length=60, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_1")
>>> timeline.add_events(
...     [{"id": "beat:1", "instant": 0.0}, {"id": "beat:2", "instant": 55.0}]
... )
>>> out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> timeline.export_to_csv(str(out / "timestamps.csv"))
2
```

```python
>>> # Tab-separated, no header
>>> timeline.export_to_csv(str(out / "data.tsv"), sep="\t", header=False)
2
```

### from_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.from_dict }

```python
timelines.Timeline.from_dict(data)
```

Create a Timeline from a dictionary.

Every coordinate dictionary in *data* — ``length``, the child
``offset``s, and the event coordinate structs — is decoded by
:func:`~timetoalign.core.retrieval.coordinate_from_dict`, so an exact ratio
comes back as a ``Fraction`` and an inexact one as a ``float``.
Feeding the result back through :meth:`to_dict` with the same
flags reproduces the input dictionary.

The ``"events"`` and ``"external_references"`` keys are optional:
a dictionary produced without them reconstructs a timeline with
zero events and an empty reference table. External references are
restored without event validation, so a payload carrying
references but no events round-trips intact.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|------------|
| data   | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Dictionary from to_dict(). | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                             | Description              |
|--------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|
|        | [Self](`typing_extensions.Self`) | A new Timeline instance. |

### get_boundary_table { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_boundary_table }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_boundary_table(
    conversion_maps=True,
    recursion_limit=None,
)
```

Get timestamps for timeline boundaries only.

Returns a timestamp table containing only start (0) and end (length)
coordinates for this timeline and all children.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                            | Default   |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | C-Maps to include as fields (see get_timestamp_table). | `True`    |
| recursion_limit | [int](`int`) \| None                                                  | Maximum depth for child traversal.                     | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                     | Description                             |
|--------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) | PyArrow Table with boundary timestamps. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=60, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_1")
>>> child = Timeline(length=10, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_2")
>>> parent.add_child(child, offset=50)
>>> parent.get_boundary_table().column_names
['cpt_1', 'cpt_2']
```

Cells are coordinate structs, so read them through the frame lane
rather than ``to_pandas()`` — the latter hands back one dict per
cell:

```python
>>> parent.get_timestamp_table(
...     parent._collect_boundary_coordinates(),
...     include_events=False,
...     format="dataframe",
...     units=False,
... )
   cpt_1  cpt_2
0    0.0    NaN
1   50.0    0.0
2   60.0   10.0
```

### get_conversion_map { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_conversion_map }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_conversion_map(target_unit)
```

Get a conversion map by target unit **or** by name/id.

When *target_unit* is a valid `TimeUnit` value (or an alias such as
``"seconds"``), the method returns the attached map targeting that
unit — and raises when several do, because picking one of two
readings of the same axis is the caller's decision, not this
method's.

When *target_unit* is a string that does **not** correspond to any
``TimeUnit`` member, the method falls back to a name-based lookup:
it searches first by ``cmap.id``, then by ``cmap.name``.  This is
useful for maps where source and target units are identical (e.g. a
``ShiftMap`` named ``"raw_quarters"`` that maps normalised quarters
back to raw partitura quarters).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                    | Description                                                                     | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| target_unit | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) | A ``TimeUnit`` member, a unit alias string, or a conversion-map name/id string. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                             | Description                                             |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ConversionMap](`timetoalign.maps.ConversionMap`)\[[Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | A matching ``ConversionMap``, or ``None`` if not found. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If several attached maps target the requested unit. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> timeline.get_conversion_map(TimeUnit.seconds)
ScalarMap(...)
>>> timeline.get_conversion_map("raw_quarters")
ShiftMap(offset=-0.5, ...)
```

Dispatch a positional or event-key coordinate query.

| at          | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) | Scalar or plural coordinate position or event key. | _required_        |

### get_event { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_event }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_event(event_id)
```

Look up a single event by its ``id`` field.

Searches this timeline's events first, then recursively searches
all children. When found in a child, coordinates are adjusted to
the root timeline's coordinate system.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type         | Description                         | Default    |
|----------|--------------|-------------------------------------|------------|
| event_id | [str](`str`) | The event identifier to search for. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                        | Description                                                 |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | A dictionary representing the event row, or ``None`` if not |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] \| None | found anywhere in the hierarchy.                            |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> event = timeline.get_event("notes:note:000001")
>>> event["id"]
'notes:note:000001'
>>> timeline.get_event("nonexistent") is None
True
```

### get_events { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_events }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_events(
    temporal_type=None,
    event_type=None,
    include_children=True,
    min_coord=None,
    max_coord=None,
    **field_filters,
)
```

Filter and retrieve events.

When ``include_children=True`` (the default), events from all
children are included with their coordinates adjusted to the
root timeline's coordinate system. Segment events (internal
bookkeeping) are always excluded.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                             | Description                                                                                                                                 | Default   |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| temporal_type    | [Literal](`typing.Literal`)\[\'instant\', \'interval\'\] \| None | Filter by "instant" or "interval".                                                                                                          | `None`    |
| event_type       | [str](`str`) \| None                                             | Filter by event type name.                                                                                                                  | `None`    |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)                                                   | If True (default), include events from all children with root-relative coordinates.                                                         | `True`    |
| min_coord        | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| None      | Minimum coordinate (inclusive). Can be a float in native units or a `Coordinate` with a different unit (converted via inverse C-Map).       | `None`    |
| max_coord        | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| None      | Maximum coordinate (exclusive). Same conversion rules as min_coord.                                                                         | `None`    |
| **field_filters  | [Any](`typing.Any`)                                              | Additional field equality filters. Each kwarg name is a field name, and the value is the required value (or a list of values for OR logic). | `{}`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                         | Description                                    |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | A filtered EventData with all matching events. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Filter by coordinate range
>>> events = tl.get_events(min_coord=10.0, max_coord=20.0)
```

```python
>>> # Filter with a Coordinate in a different unit
>>> from timetoalign import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> coord = Coordinate(5.0, TimeUnit.seconds)
>>> events = tl.get_events(min_coord=coord)
```

```python
>>> # Arbitrary field filters
>>> events = tl.get_events(pitch=60)  # Only middle C
>>> events = tl.get_events(pitch=[60, 62, 64])  # C, D, E
```

### get_events_at { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_events_at }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_events_at(coord, tolerance=0.0, include_children=True)
```

Get all events active at a specific coordinate.

Returns events from this timeline and all children that are
active (containing or at) the specified coordinate.

For instant events, an event is "at" the coordinate if its instant
is within tolerance of the query coordinate.

For interval events, an event is "active" if the coordinate falls
within [start, end).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                | Description                                       | Default    |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coord            | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | Coordinate to query (in this timeline's unit).    | _required_ |
| tolerance        | [float](`float`)                                    | Tolerance for instant event matching (default 0). | `0.0`      |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True, include events from children.            | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                  | Description                                                           |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\]\] | Dict mapping timeline_id to list of events active at that coordinate. |
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [list](`list`)\[[dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\]\]\] | Child events have coordinates in their local coordinate system.       |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> events = score.get_events_at(50.0)
>>> events["score:1"]  # Events in root at coord 50
[{"id": "n1", "event_type": "Note", ...}]
>>> events["measure_5"]  # Events in measure 5
[...]
```

### get_interval_stamp { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_interval_stamp }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_interval_stamp(
    start,
    end,
    unit=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,

```

Get a TimeIntervalStamp for a coordinate range.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                               | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| start           | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)                   | Start coordinate.                                         | _required_ |
| end             | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)                   | End coordinate.                                           | _required_ |
| unit            | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) \| None       | If provided, interpret both coords as being in this unit. | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | C-Maps available through the returned stamps.             | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                | Description                                      |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeIntervalStamp`) | TimeIntervalStamp with start and end TimeStamps. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=20, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="timeline:1")
>>> child = Timeline(length=15, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_2")
>>> parent.add_child(child, offset=0)
>>> interval = parent.get_interval_stamp(0.0, 10.0)
>>> interval.duration
Duration(10.0, seconds)
>>> interval.get_interval("cpt_2")
Interval(start=Coordinate(0.0, seconds), end=Coordinate(10.0, seconds))
```

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_regions_at(coord)
```

Return all regions containing the given coordinate.

A region contains coord if region.start <= coord < region.end
(left-inclusive, right-exclusive).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description              | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|------------|
| coord  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | The coordinate to query. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                               | Description                                               |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | List of Region objects containing coord, ordered by start |
|        | [list](`list`)\[[Region](`timetoalign.timelines.regions.Region`)\] | coordinate. Empty list if no regions contain coord.       |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

>>> tl.get_regions_at(75.0)
