
### get_slice { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_slice }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_slice(
    start,
    end,
    *,
    truncate_events=True,
    include_children=True,
    copy_cmaps=True,
)
```

Extract a portion of this timeline as a new, independent timeline.

Returns a new timeline containing all events within [start, end).
The returned timeline has its coordinate origin at 0, with all
coordinates shifted by -start.

Slicing creates a new timeline that is a structural copy of the
specified interval of the source.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name             | Type                                                | Description                                                                                                                                              | Default    |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| start            | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | Start coordinate (inclusive).                                                                                                                            | _required_ |
| end              | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | End coordinate (exclusive).                                                                                                                              | _required_ |
| truncate_events  | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True (default), interval events straddling the slice boundaries are clipped to [start, end). If False, events must be fully contained to be included. | `True`     |
| include_children | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True (default), child timelines whose span overlaps [start, end) are recursively sliced and included.                                                 | `True`     |
| copy_cmaps       | [bool](`bool`)                                      | If True (default), ConversionMaps are bounded-copied for the slice range.                                                                                | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                      |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | New Timeline (same concrete subclass) with length = end - start, |
|        | \'Timeline\' | coordinates shifted to [0, end-start).                           |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                           |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If start >= end or either is outside timeline bounds. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> source = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=100)
>>> source.add_events([
...     {"event_type": "Note", "start": 10, "end": 30},
...     {"event_type": "Beat", "instant": 25},
... ])
>>> sliced = source.get_slice(20, 40)
>>> sliced.length.value  # 40 - 20 = 20
Fraction(20, 1)
```

| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Result-axis validator.                             | `None`     |
| unit            | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) \| None                                                                                                                                                             | Optional unit for a positional query.              | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                       | C-Maps available through the returned stamps.      | `True`     |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

### get_timestamp_at { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_at }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_at(
    at,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    unit=None,
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get a TimeStamp at one coordinate on this timeline.

This is the primary coordinate resolution API. The TimeStamp provides
access to all equivalent coordinates across children and C-Map units.
The axis is written in this timeline's declared ``number_type``, so a
query of ``9.5`` on a fraction-canonical timeline gives an axis of
``Fraction(19, 2)``. Descendants are reached by exact offset
arithmetic.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| at              | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`)       | Coordinate value. Can be: - int/float/Fraction: Value in timeline's native unit - Coordinate: Must match unit or specify via `unit` param - IdCoordinate: May name this timeline or a descendant | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Result-axis validator. ``None`` or this timeline's own ID; any other ID raises.                                                                                                                  | `None`     |
| unit            | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`) \| None       | If provided, interpret ``at`` as being in this unit. The coordinate is first converted via inverse C-Map.                                                                                        | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | C-Maps available through the returned stamp.                                                                                                                                                     | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                   |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | TimeStamp object for the resolved coordinate. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                       |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If ``timeline_id`` names another timeline.        |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If unit specified but no inverse C-Map available. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.maps import TableMap
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=960, unit=TimeUnit.ticks, uid="timeline:1")
>>> child_a = Timeline(length=200, unit=TimeUnit.ticks, uid="child_a")
>>> parent.add_child(child_a, offset=100)
>>> tempo_map = TableMap(
...     x_values=[0, 960], y_values=[0.0, 2.0],
...     source_unit=TimeUnit.ticks, target_unit=TimeUnit.seconds,
... )
>>> parent.add_conversion_map(tempo_map)
>>> ts = parent.get_timestamp_at(250)
>>> ts.get_coordinate_for("child_a", format="float")
150.0
```

```python
>>> # Query with unit conversion
>>> ts = parent.get_timestamp_at(1.5, unit=TimeUnit.seconds)
>>> ts.axis  # Converted from seconds to timeline's native unit (ticks)
IdCoordinate(720, ticks, 'timeline:1')
```

### get_timestamp_for { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_for }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_for(
    key,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get the timestamp for a specific event by its ID.

Returns a TimeStamp for instant events, or a TimeIntervalStamp for
interval events. Searches recursively through children if the event
is not found on this timeline directly.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                            | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| key             | [str](`str`)                                                          | The event identifier to look up.                       | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Result-axis validator.                                 | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | C-Maps available through the returned stamp or stamps. | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                                                       | Description                                                          |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) \| [TimeIntervalStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeIntervalStamp`) | TimeStamp for instant events, TimeIntervalStamp for interval events. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                                                                         |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no event with the given ID exists, or if ``timeline_id`` names another timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=20, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="timeline:1")
>>> child = Timeline(length=10, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="clt_1")
>>> parent.add_child(child, offset=5)
>>> parent.add_events([{"event_type": "Note", "instant": 5.0}])
>>> child.add_events(
...     [{"id": "clt_1:note:000001", "event_type": "Note", "start": 0.0, "end": 2.5}]
... )
>>> ts = parent.get_timestamp_for("note:000001")
>>> ts.axis  # For instant events
IdCoordinate(5.0, seconds, 'timeline:1')
```

```python
>>> ts = parent.get_timestamp_for("clt_1:note:000001")
>>> ts.start.axis  # For interval events
IdCoordinate(5.0, seconds, 'timeline:1')
>>> ts.end.axis
IdCoordinate(7.5, seconds, 'timeline:1')
```

### get_timestamp_table { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_table }

```python
timelines.Timeline.get_timestamp_table(
    at=None,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
    recursion_limit=None,
    include_events=True,
    include_boundaries=False,
    format='table',
    fields=None,
    units=None,
    include_ids=None,
)
```

Generate a timestamp table for this timeline hierarchy.

A Timestamp is a cross-section through the timeline hierarchy showing
synchronous coordinates. This method computes local coordinates for
each timeline in the hierarchy at each axis coordinate.

Supports IdCoordinate for automatic child offset resolution: naming a
child in the query places the position on the parent axis for you.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name               | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default   |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| at                 | [CoordinateInput](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateInput`) \| [CoordinateCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.CoordinateCollection`) \| [str](`str`) \| [KeyCollection](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.KeyCollection`) \| None | Explicit positions to use as the axis, or event IDs (one row per event, in the order given). If None, coordinates are extracted from events (and optionally boundaries). Accepts IdCoordinate objects - if timeline_id matches a child, the offset is automatically applied.                         | `None`    |
| conversion_maps    | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                                                                                                                                                               | C-Maps to include as fields. Flexible input: - True: Include all attached conversion maps - str: Map ID or target unit name (e.g., "inches", "seconds") - TimeUnit: Find map by target unit enum - ConversionMap: Include the specific map - list: Mix of the above - None/False: No conversion maps | `True`    |
| recursion_limit    | [int](`int`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Maximum depth for child traversal. None = unlimited.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `None`    |
| include_events     | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True and ``at`` is None, extract from events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `True`    |
| include_boundaries | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | If True, include timeline boundary coordinates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `False`   |
| format             | [TableFormat](`timetoalign.core.retrieval.TableFormat`)                                                                                                                                                                             | ``"table"`` (default) for a PyArrow table, ``"dataframe"`` for a pandas DataFrame.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `'table'` |
| fields             | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\'                                                                                                                                                           | How to name the DataFrame fields (``format="dataframe"``): - None or ColumnNaming.name (default): Use timeline/cmap name - ColumnNaming.id: Use timeline/cmap id - Callable: Function taking (name, metadata_dict) -> new_name - list[str]: Explicit field names                                     | `None`    |
| units              | [bool](`bool`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                              | If True (the DataFrame default), append units to field names like "name (unit)".                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `None`    |
| include_ids        | [bool](`bool`) \| None                                                                                                                                                                                                              | If True (the DataFrame default), add event IDs as the DataFrame index when coordinates are collected from events.                                                                                                                                                                                    | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | With ``format="table"``, a PyArrow Table whose fields are                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | coordinate structs, one per timeline plus one per C-Map: - {timeline_id}: local coordinate per timeline, this one   first (carrying the queried positions themselves), then   each child; nullable where a timeline does not reach a row - {cmap_name}: converted value per C-Map |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | There is no separate ``axis`` field: this timeline's own column                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | already holds those positions, and a duplicate of it would be a                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | second name for one thing. (Unrelated to ``Stamp.axis``, which is                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | a stamp's typed source coordinate and keeps its name.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | Each field includes metadata: - unit: TimeUnit.value string (e.g., "seconds", "pixels") - number_type: the representation the column declares - timeline_id: Timeline ID (for timeline fields) - cmap_id: C-Map ID (for C-Map fields)                                             |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | Metadata lives in the versioned blob, so read it through                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | ``field_metadata(table.schema.field(col_name))`` rather than by                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | indexing ``.metadata`` with a bare key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | With ``format="dataframe"``, the same data as a pandas DataFrame                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | with one scalar per cell, written in the representation each                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|        | [pa](`pyarrow`).[Table](`pyarrow.Table`) \| [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | column declares.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                   |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | On an unknown ``format``, or when a DataFrame-shaping option is supplied for an Arrow result. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import IdCoordinate, TimeUnit
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline
>>> parent = Timeline(length=60, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_1")
>>> child = Timeline(length=10, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, uid="cpt_2")
>>> parent.add_child(child, offset=50)
>>> parent.add_events([{"id": "beat:1", "instant": 0.0}])
>>> parent.get_timestamp_table().column_names
['cpt_1', 'cpt_2']
```

Every column names the timeline it belongs to; metadata lives in
the versioned blob:

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core.fields import field_metadata
>>> field_metadata(parent.get_timestamp_table().schema.field("cpt_1"))["unit"]
'seconds'
```

A child position is placed on the parent axis automatically:

```python
>>> coords = [IdCoordinate(v, TimeUnit.seconds, "cpt_2") for v in (0.0, 5.0)]
>>> parent.get_timestamp_table(coords, format="dataframe", units=False)
   cpt_1  cpt_2
0   50.0    0.0
1   55.0    5.0
```

### lock { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.lock }

```python
timelines.Timeline.lock()
```

Lock this timeline so that it can no longer expand.

The timeline enters the state ``locked=True`` gives at construction:
content and children must fit its length, and appending refuses. A
root that grows by appending, such as a segment line, is locked this
way once built. Locking a locked timeline (a child, for instance)
changes nothing. A lock cannot be lifted.

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     SegmentLine,
... )
>>> line = SegmentLine[ContinuousLogicalTimeline](length=0, unit="quarters")
>>> line.append_segment(ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=4, unit="quarters"))
>>> line.append_segment(ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=2, unit="quarters"))
>>> line.is_locked
False
>>> line.lock()
>>> line.is_locked
True
```

### resolve_subclass { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.resolve_subclass }

```python
timelines.Timeline.resolve_subclass(unit, number_type=None)
```

Return the most specific Timeline subclass for a unit/number_type pair.

Inspects all subclasses and selects the one whose
``_allowed_units`` includes *unit*.  Among candidates the selection
prefers, in order:

1. A class whose default unit uses *number_type* (when supplied).
2. The class with the **smallest** ``_allowed_units`` set (most
   specific domain).

Further-derived subclasses participate in the lookup and can be
selected when they are the most specific matching candidate.

Falls back to the base ``Timeline`` if no subclass claims the unit.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| unit        | [TimeUnit](`timetoalign.core.TimeUnit`) \| [str](`str`)             | The time unit to look up.                                                                                                                      | _required_ |
| number_type | [NumberType](`timetoalign.core.NumberType`) \| [str](`str`) \| None | Optional number type for disambiguation (e.g. ``NumberType.fraction`` selects a fractional logical timeline over ``DiscreteLogicalTimeline``). | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                | Description                                              |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [type](`type`)\[[Timeline](`timetoalign.timelines.base.Timeline`)\] | The most specific Timeline subclass that accepts *unit*. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> Timeline.resolve_subclass(TimeUnit.quarters, NumberType.fraction)
<class 'timetoalign.timelines.types.ContinuousLogicalTimeline'>
>>> Timeline.resolve_subclass(TimeUnit.pixels)
<class 'timetoalign.timelines.types.DiscreteGraphicalTimeline'>
```

### to_dict { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.to_dict }

```python
timelines.Timeline.to_dict(events=False, external_references=False)
```

Convert timeline to a dictionary for serialization.

The default output is the timeline's complete structure: its axis,
children, conversion maps, regions, measure map, metric hierarchy,
and flow control. ``"events"`` and ``"external_references"`` are
**absent** unless explicitly requested. This structural payload is
called the eventless payload: it preserves authored structure without
carrying event rows. Structure is not inferred for slices, children
created from regions, or unfolded timelines.

Coordinate-valued members — ``length`` and every child
``offset`` — are emitted as canonical coordinate dictionaries
(:func:`~timetoalign.core.retrieval.coordinate_to_dict`), so the result is
JSON-serializable whatever the timeline's number type, and
``Fraction`` coordinates survive the round trip exactly.

Collections are written in one canonical order, independent of the
order in which their content was added, so equal timelines give equal
JSON text: ``children`` by offset, then id; ``conversion_maps`` by id;
``regions`` by start, then end, then id; and in ``flow_control``
(:meth:`~timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol.FlowControlRegistry.to_dict`)
``breaks`` and ``markers`` by coordinate, ``jumps`` by from and then
to coordinate, each then by id.
Coordinates compare by exact numeric value and strings by Unicode code
point (:func:`~timetoalign.core.retrieval.canonical_order`). Every
other member keeps its order. The timeline's own storage is not
reordered, and :meth:`from_dict` accepts any order.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Default   |
|---------------------|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| events              | [bool](`bool`) | If True, include an ``"events"`` key holding this timeline's event rows.                                                                                                                                                 | `False`   |
| external_references | [bool](`bool`) | If True, include an ``"external_references"`` key holding the reference table as a list of row dicts (``access_points`` as a nested list of ``{"uri": ..., "kind": ...}`` dicts). Included even when the table is empty. | `False`   |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A JSON-serializable dictionary representation of the timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> "events" in tl.to_dict()
False
>>> "events" in tl.to_dict(events=True)
True
```

### to_typed { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.to_typed }

```python
timelines.Timeline.to_typed()
```

Return this timeline re-instantiated as the appropriate typed subclass.

Uses the timeline's unit and number type to determine the correct
concrete subclass (e.g., ``ContinuousPhysicalTimeline`` for seconds/float).
If the timeline is already an instance of the correct subclass, returns
``self`` unchanged.

This is useful after deserialization (e.g., ``Timeline.from_dict()``) or
when working with generic ``Timeline`` instances that should carry
domain-specific type information.

Events, external references, conversion maps, regions, flow maps, and
metadata are preserved. Children are recursively re-typed.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                        |
|--------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | A Timeline instance of the appropriate typed subclass, or ``self`` |
|        | \'Timeline\' | if it is already the correct type.                                 |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> tl = Timeline(length=10.0, unit=TimeUnit.seconds)
>>> typed = tl.to_typed()
>>> type(typed).__name__
'ContinuousPhysicalTimeline'
>>> typed.is_continuous
True
```

```python
>>> # Already typed -- returns self
>>> cpt = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0)
>>> cpt.to_typed() is cpt
True
```

### validate_child { #timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.validate_child }

```python
timelines.Timeline.validate_child(child, offset)
```

Validate that a timeline can be added as a child.

A timeline can accommodate events and other timelines, called
Children, as long as they use the same measuring unit.

For cross-domain relationships (e.g., physical to logical), use
TimelineGroup instead of parent-child nesting.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                    | Default    |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------|
| child  | [Timeline](`timetoalign.timelines.base.Timeline`)   | The timeline to validate.      | _required_ |
| offset | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) | The proposed start coordinate. | _required_ |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                               |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TypeError](`TypeError`)   | If child is not a Timeline.                                               |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If units don't match or the timeline already is a child of this timeline. |
